ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

wrist — clinical pattern 2

A patient has persistent dorsal wrist pain and clicking after a fall. Stress radiographs show abnormal widening between the scaphoid and lunate, without a scaphoid fracture or displacement of the lunate from the radius. Which ligamentous injury best explains the finding?

  1. Triangular fibrocartilage complex injury
  2. Perilunate dislocation
  3. Lunate dislocation
  4. Scapholunate ligament injury
  5. Scaphoid fracture
Answer and explanation

Scapholunate ligament injury

Scapholunate dissociation widens the interval between the scaphoid and lunate and can cause dorsal wrist pain or instability.

Option explanations

Scapholunate ligament injury: Scapholunate dissociation widens the interval between the scaphoid and lunate and can cause dorsal wrist pain or instability.

Scaphoid fracture: Focal snuffbox or scaphoid-tubercle tenderness after a fall raises concern for scaphoid fracture even when initial films are negative. This is not the pattern specified in this case.

Triangular fibrocartilage complex injury: The TFCC supports the ulnar wrist and distal radioulnar joint; injury can produce ulnar-sided pain and pain with rotation. This is not the pattern specified in this case.

Perilunate dislocation: The lunate remains aligned with the radius while the capitate and remaining carpus are displaced, commonly dorsally. This is not the pattern specified in this case.

Lunate dislocation: The lunate itself displaces, typically volarly, losing its normal relationship with the distal radius and capitate. This is not the pattern specified in this case.
